# SPD-059 — Bash hook: an alias defined on the line and run through eval hides a command (Law 7)

## Brief
The same class as SPD-054: the line stores code the hook never reads. `alias gp='git push'` is kind other with no finding, and a later `eval gp` on the same line runs the alias body; analyse_words keeps no alias table, so eval's reading of `gp` finds an ordinary command word. A fix would record an alias name and body the way SPD-043 records a variable and read the body where the name is dispatched; an alias is expanded at parse time, so only eval, a sourced file and a nested shell reach it on the same line. (Burbank's Why, restored by Spud from his log: a stray second `--why ''` cleared the proposal's.)

Evidence: Probed from the SPD-054 scratchpad with a fake git first on a scratch PATH (bash 3.2, zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, sh): `alias gp='git push'; eval gp` ran git push in zsh, zsh-nbgq and sh; bash 3.2 did not (it expands no alias non-interactively without expand_aliases). `alias g=git; g push` ran in none of the four, because alias expansion happens when the whole line is parsed, before the alias exists. The hook on this branch reads `alias gp='git push'; eval gp` as kinds other,eval,other with no finding, for a member. zsh's TRAP<SIG> function form (`TRAPEXIT() { git push; }`, `function TRAPEXIT { git push; }`, probed: ran in both zsh readings) is NOT a hole: the hook already analyses function bodies and finds the git push.

## Size, persona and model decision
Batch plan v2, wave 1 with SPD-061 and SPD-060, same engineer on opus. The alias table goes on ShellAnalysis in shell/syntax.py and is read where eval re-analyses its words in shell/analyse.py, the shape SPD-043 used for a variable.
